sample_unit: ICU episodes (one summary per LLM per episode)

links.outcome: LLM ICU summary capture of key clinical events and hallucinations, adjudicated by intensivists
links.effect: Key event identification was 41.5 ± 15.2% for GPT-4 API, 19.2 ± 20.9% for ChatGPT and 16.5 ± 14.1% for Llama2 (p = 0.002). GPT-4 API produced minor hallucinations.
links.quote: Overall ability to identify a pre-defined list of important clinical events in the summary was 41.5 ± 15.2% for GPT-4 API, 19.2 ± 20.9% for ChatGPT and 16.5 ± 14.1% for Llama2 (p = 0.002).

links.outcome: Performance of LLM summaries on intended-use ICU discharge summary task with local data
links.effect: All models had narrative coherence problems and omitted key clinical data; only moderately captured clinically meaningful data in correct order.
links.quote: All encountered issues with narrative coherence and omitted key clinical data and only moderately captured all clinically meaningful data in the correct order.

screen.reason: Empirical feasibility study evaluating LLMs (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Llama 2) for generating ICU discharge summaries from retrospective records, adjudicated by intensivists without testing a specific deployment practice/safeguard.
